baseline: rooftop-weathering-04/terrace-book.pxo and terrace-book.png. Entire 04 source retained as the before version.
referenceReading: The station pillars carry adjoining light and dark grey-green old-pigment fields; narrow local bright abrasion reveals old plaster, and a few deeper areas remain in recesses.

The platform floor retains structural grout direction while unequal patching and layer remnants cross adjacent pixel clusters. These material levels remain readable in the scene, not solely at a texture zoom.
paintChanges: Increase actual non-base pigment coverage from 04 approximate 2–6% to 05 27–34%. Each of the six repainted material fields contains exactly six deliberate native colours.
Build joined old-pigment masses with broken square stepped edges, base-colour erosion incursions, lighter/mineral upper remnants and locally recessed grey-green underlayers.

Offset secondary layers toward eroded edges instead of placing a contrasting core in every mark. Several adjacent source clusters join into a larger old-layer relation; north and south use different main layouts.
Keep fine 1 px dark structural joint fragments and connected repair fissures. Warm old mortar is restricted to a few repair cores, and small mineral grains are associated with larger eroded edges.
The wall plaster palette is lighter than the floor; cap stone is paler still. Cement remains a middle grey-green mineral material. The 04 metal and rust-iron paintings are preserved exactly.
The 1 px source unit and existing 16 px/m mapping remain unchanged. No geometry, UV, camera, atmosphere, runtime or lighting file was modified by the painting task.
referenceUse: Viewed supplied reference only. No copied, generated, traced or downscaled reference bitmap. Python describes explicit strokes; actual raster painting, native save, PNG export and review crops were performed inside Pixelorama.
